name: CI

# OXIDE v2: runs exactly `mise run verify` — the same command used locally
# (Ruff, mypy --strict, pytest over the Python engine; ADR-0011).
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, rewrite/v2]
  push:
    branches: [main]

# One run per change: PR runs cancel when superseded; main pushes (run_id) never do.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Install pinned uv
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
        with:
          version: 2026.9.14
          install_args: uv
      - name: Restore the ContextBench corpora cache
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/oxide
          key: oxide-cache-linux-x86_64-${{ hashFiles('src/oxide/storage/ladybug.py', 'fixtures/eval/contextbench-py/tasks.json') }}
      # The corpora stay cached; the FTS build is always fetched cold, so a replaced
      # upstream build cannot hide behind the cache (docs/fts-mirror/RELEASE.md).
      - name: Drop the cached FTS extension
        run: rm -f ~/.cache/oxide/ladybug-extensions-*/libfts.lbug_extension
      - name: Install locked environment, verify the FTS extension, fetch the corpora
        run: mise run bootstrap
      - name: mise run verify
        run: mise run verify
        env:
          MISE_AUTO_INSTALL: "false"
          # Parallel in CI only; loadfile keeps a file's shared corpora fixture in one worker.
          PYTEST_ADDOPTS: -n auto --dist loadfile
name: Platforms

# Cross-platform verification of the Python engine (docs/platforms.md): on every
# supported platform, the locked environment installs, `oxide prepare` fetches that
# platform's pinned FTS build, mypy and the test suite run from the checkout, and the
# built wheel and sdist pass scripts/smoke_dist.py from a fresh environment.
# ContextBench quality gates stay in ci.yml (Linux) and `mise run contextbench-ts`.
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, rewrite/v2]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

# One run per change: PR runs cancel when superseded; main pushes (run_id) never do.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  platform:
    name: ${{ matrix.label }}
    # Intel macOS is the slowest runner (retired by GitHub in 2027): it runs on main
    # pushes and manual runs, not on PRs. The label picks the runner, so exclude works.
    runs-on: >-
      ${{ fromJSON('{"windows-x86_64": "windows-2025", "macos-x86_64": "macos-15-intel",
      "macos-arm64": "macos-15"}')[matrix.label] || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # ladybug 0.21.0's macOS wheels need macOS 15 or later.
        label: [linux-x86_64, windows-x86_64, macos-x86_64, macos-arm64,
                linux-x86_64-py3.12, linux-x86_64-py3.14]
        # The ends of requires-python; the other rows use .python-version (3.13).
        include:
          - { label: linux-x86_64-py3.12, python: "3.12" }
          - { label: linux-x86_64-py3.14, python: "3.14" }
        exclude:
          - label: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'macos-x86_64' || 'none' }}
    env:
      UV_PYTHON: ${{ matrix.python }}  # empty: .python-version
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      # Fixtures and frozen spans are byte-exact: no CRLF conversion on Windows.
      - run: git config --global core.autocrlf false
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Install pinned uv
        uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
        with:
          version: 2026.9.14
          install_args: uv
      # Windows prerequisite (docs/platforms.md): ladybug's wheel excludes OpenSSL 3.
      - name: OpenSSL 3 DLLs in the system directory
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          dll=$(ls /c/Program\ Files/OpenSSL*/bin/libssl-3-x64.dll 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)
          if [ -z "$dll" ]; then
            choco install -y --no-progress openssl
            dll=$(ls /c/Program\ Files/OpenSSL*/bin/libssl-3-x64.dll | head -n 1)
          fi
          cp "$dll" "$(dirname "$dll")/libcrypto-3-x64.dll" /c/Windows/System32/
      # Not cached: every run fetches the pinned FTS build cold, so a replaced or missing
      # upstream build fails here instead of hiding behind a cache (docs/fts-mirror/RELEASE.md).
      - name: Install the locked environment and the FTS extension
        run: |
          uv sync --locked
          uv run --locked oxide prepare
          uv run --locked python scripts/smoke_dist.py --environment | tee environment.json
      - name: mypy --strict (this platform's branches)
        run: uv run --locked mypy
      - name: pytest (without the ContextBench corpora gate)
        run: >
          uv run --locked pytest --ignore=tests/python/test_contextbench.py
          --ignore=tests/python/test_contextbench_ts.py
          --junitxml=pytest.xml
        env:
          PYTEST_ADDOPTS: -n auto --dist loadfile
      - name: Build the wheel and sdist
        run: uv build --out-dir dist
      # A lock can hide what a user's pip picks from the wheel's own metadata:
      # by default pip takes the newest release even when it has only an sdist.
      - name: Install the wheel with pip from its own metadata
        run: |
          venv="$RUNNER_TEMP/pip-wheel"
          uv venv -q --seed "$venv"
          python="$venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$python" ] || python="$venv/Scripts/python.exe"
          wheel=$(ls dist/*.whl)
          "$python" -m pip install -q --dry-run --ignore-installed --report "$RUNNER_TEMP/pip.json" "$wheel"
          "$python" -I -c "
          import json, sys
          report = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'))['install']
          built = [f\"{i['metadata']['name']} {i['metadata']['version']}\" for i in report
                   if not i['download_info']['url'].endswith('.whl')]
          sys.exit(f'pip would build from source: {built}' if built else 0)" "$RUNNER_TEMP/pip.json"
          "$python" -m pip install -q --only-binary :all: "$wheel"
          "$python" -m pip check
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP" && "$python" -I "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/smoke_dist.py" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fixtures")
      - name: Smoke-test each artifact in a fresh environment
        run: |
          uv export --locked --no-dev --no-emit-project --no-hashes -q -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
          for artifact in dist/*.whl dist/*.tar.gz; do
            venv="$RUNNER_TEMP/smoke-$(basename "$artifact")"
            uv venv -q "$venv"
            # Third-party dependencies must ship wheels; only OXIDE's sdist is built.
            uv pip install -q --python "$venv" --only-binary :all: -r "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements.txt"
            uv pip install -q --python "$venv" --no-deps "$artifact"
            uv pip check --python "$venv"
            python="$venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$python" ] || python="$venv/Scripts/python.exe"
            echo "== $artifact"
            (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP" && "$python" -I "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/scripts/smoke_dist.py" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fixtures")
          done
      - name: Keep the platform record
        # act (local runs) cannot copy this action into podman containers.
        if: always() && !env.ACT
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v5
        with:
          name: platform-${{ matrix.label }}
          path: |
            environment.json
            pytest.xml
            dist/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

# supported platform, the locked environment installs, `oxide prepare` fetches that
# platform's pinned FTS build, mypy and the test suite run from the checkout, and the

  push:
    branches: [main]

# One run per change: PR runs cancel when superseded; main pushes (run_id) never do.

      ${{ fromJSON('{"windows-x86_64": "windows-2025", "macos-x86_64": "macos-15-intel",
      "macos-arm64": "macos-15"}')[matrix.label] || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}

                linux-x86_64-py3.12, linux-x86_64-py3.14]

          - { label: linux-x86_64-py3.14, python: "3.14" }

      UV_PYTHON: ${{ matrix.python }}  # empty: .python-version
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      # Fixtures and frozen spans are byte-exact: no CRLF conversion on Windows.
      - run: git config --global core.autocrlf false
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

**What the runs showed** (Platforms run 41298189655 and others)
- **Windows pytest is the slowest step** at about 395s, against 45–53s on Linux. Most of the gap is fsync calls in the storage layer: each costs about 85ms on the Windows runner, and the suite makes about 7,100 of them. That correlates at 0.80 with the extra Windows time per test. Defender is already off on `windows-2025`, so it isn't the cause.
- **Installing dependencies is not a bottleneck.** `uv sync` takes 2–22s, so adding a uv cache isn't worth it.
- **The ContextBench corpora cache kept missing.** Its key included `src/oxide/storage/ladybug.py`, which changed four times in PR #45, so each change forced a cold 96s bootstrap.
- **Changing how pytest-xdist splits tests across workers wouldn't help.** A simulated ideal split comes out the same (318s vs 317s).
- **Linux x86_64 was checked twice per run:** ci.yml's Verify job and Platforms' `linux-x86_64` row both ran mypy and pytest.

**Changes (uncommitted)**
1. **`tests/python/conftest.py`:** a new `no_fsync` fixture applies to every test and turns off `_fsync` inside the test process. No test can observe durability anyway. Tests that start subprocesses (crash injection, CLI, `smoke_dist.py`) still flush for real, so recovery coverage stays. Expected result: Windows pytest drops from about 395s to well under half (estimated, not measured), and macOS Intel also gets faster.
2. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`:**
   - The cache now holds only `~/.cache/oxide/contextbench`, keyed on `tasks.json`.
   - I removed the step that deleted the FTS build, because the FTS build is no longer in the cache. It is still fetched cold on every run, so that release gate is unchanged.

I pushed the branch `ci/speedup`. The Platforms run passes on all six platforms, Intel macOS included, and Windows tests now take 58% less time. I didn't open a PR.

**Measured: Platforms run 41312039897 vs the `main` baseline (run 41298189655)**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Windows pytest step | 395s | 149s |
| Windows tests, summed over all tests | 1270s | 531s |
| Windows TS incremental test | 155s | 30s |
| Windows reexport-chain test | 146s | 6s |
| Windows job | 568s | 305s |
| Intel macOS tests, summed | 607s | 384s |
| Intel macOS job | 343–630s | 297s |
| linux-x86_64 row | ~105–190s | 60s |

The summed per-test time fell for the same tests, so the drop isn't run-to-run noise. The cause was fsync: each flush costs about 85ms on the Windows runner, and test processes no longer flush. Tests that start subprocesses, such as crash injection, still flush for real.

**What changed** (one commit on `ci/speedup`)
- **`tests/python/conftest.py`:** the `no_fsync` fixture skips flushing in every test.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`:** the corpora cache is keyed only on `tasks.json`, so editing `ladybug.py` no longer forces a 96s cold bootstrap. The FTS build is still fetched cold on every run.
- **`.github/workflows/platforms.yml`:** the `linux-x86_64` row only builds and smoke-tests the wheel. Verify (`ubuntu-latest`) and the py3.12/3.14 rows (`ubuntu-24.04`) still run mypy and the tests.

No platform, release gate or Python version lost coverage. I reverted the `ubuntu-24.04` pin from my first pass, so Verify still runs on `ubuntu-latest`.

**Not yet measured:** the ci.yml cache change. CI only runs on PRs and on pushes to `main`, and that workflow has no manual trigger. On its first run the new key misses once, then hits until `tasks.json` changes.

**Found, not fixed:**
- On both macOS runners, two JEV judge tests (one in `test_jev`, one in `test_mcp`) take about 36s each, against 0.5s on Linux. The cause is unknown, and it may also slow down macOS users' first judge call.
- Real Windows users pay about 85ms per file during a cold index because of the per-file fsync.
